original_question: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3; 3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 18: "Is T113(n, 2n-3; 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 4?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the weighted type-113 tiling count T113(a,b;3), correctly interprets type 113 as allowing both stone orientations and all three bone orientations, uses the same peripheral diagonal (n, 2n-3), keeps the lower bound n >= 4, and asks exactly about 2-adic continuity. This is essentially Problem 18 in Section 8.
missing_details: The paper’s official notation comes from Section 1: T_{ijk}(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which the right stone is allowed iff i=1, the left stone is allowed iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations are allowed; this should be stated explicitly to anchor the meaning of type 113.
The weighted notation T_{ijk}(a,b;3) is introduced later in Section 8, with the precise rule that a tiling containing m stones contributes weight 3^m.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the variable n should be specified to range over integers n >= 4.

The phrase "2-adically continuous" is not unpacked in the paper, so a stand-alone version should define it explicitly in the standard sense: for every r >= 1 there exists s >= 1 such that n \equiv n' (mod 2^s) implies f(n) \equiv f(n') (mod 2^r).
The codomain/topology should be implicit or explicit: this is a Z-valued function viewed with the 2-adic metric, equivalently as taking values in Z_2.
The paper does not ask an eventual or asymptotic version; the quantifier is exactly the full domain n >= 4, not "for all sufficiently large n".
No ambient field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the only extra structure needed is the 2-adic topology on the integers.
refined_question: Let T_{113}(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which both right and left stones and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones contributes weight 3^m. For integers n >= 4, define f(n)=T_{113}(n,2n-3;3). Is f 2-adically continuous as a function of n; that is, for every integer r >= 1, does there exist an integer s >= 1 such that whenever n,n' >= 4 and n \equiv n' (mod 2^s), one has T_{113}(n,2n-3;3) \equiv T_{113}(n',2n'-3;3) (mod 2^r)?
justification: The draft matches Section 8’s weighted type-113 problem almost verbatim. Section 1 defines T_{ijk}(a,b) and explains that i=1 means right stones are allowed, j=1 means left stones are allowed, and k records how many bone orientations are permitted, so type 113 is exactly the all-prototiles case. Section 8 then introduces the weighted version T_{ijk}(a,b;3), where each tiling with m stones has weight 3^m, and Problem 18 asks precisely whether T_{113}(n,2n-3;3) is 2-adically continuous for n >= 4. The nearby comments about observed congruence patterns and the alternative weighting interpretation provide motivation, but they do not change the formal target of the problem.
